_note: Act III: the resolution. Frames. Templates. {UPPERCASE} slots draw a fresh atom each time; {lowercase} slots are the story's own fields ({first}, {place}, {want}...). {the_thing}, {the_someone}, {the_message}, {the_disaster} reuse something an earlier beat introduced: favored when it exists, never used when it doesn't. Tagged entries are favored in those genres. {SLOT:feature} requires a feature (see frames.py); verbs bind to the subject and object around them; {was}/{is} agree with the noun before. An entry's "ending" (a name or a list of triumph, bittersweet, tragic, open) is for those endings only; an untagged entry fits any (endings.py).

entries.text: In the end, {first} had {PRIZE:!inner} but kept {VALUE}.

{first} left {place} for good, and {CLOSE:human} did not write.

{first} {HABIT_PLACE} {landmark} every {season}, and {place} was the poorer for {LOSS}.
{first} kept {VALUE}, and {place} never forgot what it cost.
Nobody in {place} knew what became of {THING}, and {first} was not saying.
{place} was still asking about {TOPIC}, and {first} still {HABIT_PLACE} {landmark}.
